leftEvidence.title: Elijah is promised before the day of the LORD

points.label: Event action and claim
points.left: The closing oracle calls Israel to remember Moses and promises Elijah before the great day.
points.right: John tells Jerusalem’s delegation that he is not the Christ, Elijah, or the prophet, then identifies himself with Isaiah’s voice.

points.label: Response and consequence
points.left: The promised figure turns family hearts and stands before threatened judgment.
points.right: He explains his water baptism by pointing to one already standing among them.

payload.posture: Malachi promises Elijah while John says he is not Elijah.

rightEvidence.title: John denies three identities and names a present unknown one

payload.tension: Other Gospel role-language prevents either statement from being ignored or forced into a simple identity claim.
payload.title: Elijah promised and John’s denial
